alternatives.argument: The conservation form, the flux class and the Cauchy data class are fixed by the notational contract; the Kruzhkov lectures [KL] §1 and §4.1 (equations (4.2)--(4.3)) and Bressan [BCL] §1.1--1.2 state the same objects, and no step of the item uses a [KR]-specific result.

[KL] §4.1 states the weak integral identity (4.3) with the initial term, and [KL] §5.5 (5.31) fixes the strong local $L^1$ trace; [BCL] §2.1 defines weak solutions as $L^1$ classes. The local definition is representative-independent from these statements alone.

The existing [KL] §4.1 reference supplies the classical/weak equivalence and weak identity (4.3). The current local proof obtains box integration by parts coordinatewise from FTC and Fubini, with the chain rule and derivative algebra for the flux. The declared smooth cutoff lemma detects a nonzero continuous residual; under the explicitly assumed Countable Choice, injectivity of locally integrable functions in distributions identifies the initial trace as an almost-everywhere class. This supplier route uses no [KR]-specific estimate.

[KL] §5.5 Definition 5.11 with Proposition 5.12 states the exact Kruzhkov family, the nonnegative-test inequality and the strong $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ trace, and derives the weak identity; [BCL] §2.3 states the same entropy family. The definition needs no [KR] input beyond what these treatments state.

The doubling-variables inequality is proved in [KL] §5.5 (and used there for uniqueness) with the same mollifier and sign-approximation steps; the local proof uses only the two Kruzhkov inequalities of the definition and mollification, not a [KR]-specific lemma.

[KL] §5.1--5.2 derives the same jump condition (5.19')--(5.22) and its chord reformulation (Remark 5.6) from the entropy inequality by integration by parts, and [BCL] §2.3 (2.25)--(2.26) states the secant form; the local proof rests only on the Rankine--Hugoniot condition and the convexity of the entropies.

[BCL] §6.1 Theorem 4 states well-posedness and $L^1$ contractivity for the scalar problem, and [KL] §5.5 proves the local contraction from the doubling inequality; the local proof combines the Kato inequality with a cone test function, so no [KR]-specific estimate is consumed.

[BCL] §6.1 Theorem 4 gives uniqueness and the contraction; [KL] §5.5 gives the positive-part/order-preservation argument. Both directions are derived locally from the contraction estimate and monotone convergence.

[KL] §5.4 proves the $L^1$ space and time modulus estimates for the viscous problem from the equation itself; the local compactness argument re-derives the same estimates from the in-run heat bounds and the Fréchet--Kolmogorov criterion, so no [KR] lemma is needed.

[KL] §5.5--6 and [BCL] §8 treat scalar existence by vanishing viscosity/entropy limits; the local proof uses the local precompactness lemma, the viscous entropy identity and the contraction-based approximation step, none of which is [KR]-specific.
